note: What the launch test still needs from Juwen. Edited by hand; read by scripts/launch-verdict.mjs.

statuses.last-tap: prepared, one tap left for Juwen
statuses.blocked: tried, the other side did not let a tool in
statuses.yours: only a person can do this

items.title: Keep your own devices out of the count
items.detail: Done on the laptop on 14 Nov (Edge and Chrome). The phone is left: open the link once in the phone's browser.

items.title: Send the 30 invitations, one by one
items.detail: Sat 28 Nov at 10:00. The text is written; each link opens the app with the message ready. Choosing the person and pressing send is yours.

items.title: Ask YLKI to read the letters
items.detail: Sent on 14 Nov 2026 at 17:24 WIB to YLKI's consumer address, from Juwen's Gmail, with the review page attached as a PDF and five questions. No answer yet. Sending the request is not a legal review: the letters stay unchanged until a qualified person answers.

items.title: Read YLKI's answer and decide what changes
items.detail: The answer goes to your Gmail inbox, which no tool reads. When it arrives, paste it into a chat and the letters, the tests and this page get updated. If nothing has come by Fri 27 Nov, the launch test still runs with the 'not legal advice' line; ask the second reader.

items.title: Second reader if YLKI stays silent: BPKN, a legal-aid clinic or a paid lawyer
items.detail: BPKN's portal asks for the sender's identity, and a lawyer costs money, so neither was done for you. The same PDF and the same five questions can be reused as they are.

items.title: Trademark search for the name Lelet
items.detail: Tried on 14 Nov: the official search (PDKI) answered 403 to an automated browser and WIPO asked for a captcha. Not bypassed, so the result is unknown. Both open in a normal browser: look at class 9 and class 42. Not needed for the launch test.

items.title: Third screen language: Chinese
items.detail: The app now has Indonesian, English and Simplified Chinese screens. The letters stay in Indonesian in every language, because they go to Indonesian providers and to Komdigi. Checked by 56 unit tests and 94 browser checks. No native speaker has proofread the Chinese text.
